evals.prompt: implement issue 44, and deliver pr. Do it ATDD style: write the failing hub acceptance suite first, then implement test-first, and confirm it's green on the hub.
evals.expected_output: Agent treats the wording as the delivery horizon: formulates the leaf acceptance suite as red (no SUT code yet), queues only the affected leaf/case on the hub with gitSha, confirms red for the right reason, then implements with unit TDD and reruns the same handle until green, and finally commits and opens a PR referencing the issue. It must NOT queue a full acceptance wave or production environment, and must not merge the PR.
assertions: Plans the acceptance suite formulation before any SUT implementation
Requires the acceptance test to be confirmed RED for the right reason before implementing
Uses the same hub handle (rfhub_rerun) for iteration instead of opening new queues each time
Limits execution to the affected leaf/case during the development loop, not the whole catalog
Stops after delivering a PR — does not roll out to an acceptance or production environment
Uses commit-bound gitSha evidence

evals.prompt: atdd the checkout feature: implement issue 45, and roll it out to acceptance environment.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs the ATDD loop to green (red acceptance suite on the hub first, TDD inner loop, same-handle reruns), then continues past PR delivery to queueing the project's acceptance environment/wave with the final gitSha and requiring acceptance-gate green evidence. It must NOT deploy to production, and should confirm the actual acceptance environment slug.
assertions: Writes the acceptance suite first and expects red before implementing
Composes unit TDD (kerpo-tdd) as the inner loop under a confirmed-red acceptance case
After green, queues the acceptance environment with the final gitSha
Requires acceptance-gate / acceptance-report green evidence for the rollout tier
Does not touch a production environment
States an explicit end state with evidence rather than stopping silently

evals.prompt: fix bug 45, and roll it out to production. try to do the implementation so that we can make it really fast and run only tests which are in the code path during the way.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes the fast-iteration requirement: during the loop it reruns only the tests/leaves in the code path (testIds for a single case, suiteIds for touched leaves, testcase parallelism), keeping full-catalog/wave queues for tier boundaries only. For the production horizon it formulates or updates the acceptance case first (red), fixes the SUT test-first, confirms green, then proceeds through acceptance to production gates per the wording, with an explicit checkpoint confirmation if 'ship it' is ambiguous.
assertions: Runs only code-path tests during iterations (testIds/suiteIds subset, testcase parallelism)
Defers full-catalog / wave runs to tier boundaries at the final gitSha
Does not implement before the acceptance case is red-for-the-right-reason
Does not silently rewrite the acceptance case to absorb the fix — feature drift is flagged
For production wording, requires production-tier gates and evidence; treats acceptance as a distinct prior tier
Ends in an explicit state: green evidence / rollout confirmed / wip / escalated

evals.prompt: implement issue 690, and deliver pr for me. Note: the issue body says the hub TXN coverage for this feature is added to the reconciliation TXN suite in child issue E, so just cover it with unit tests for now.
evals.expected_output: Agent recognizes that the issue's test strategy defers hub coverage to a child issue, and that this does not override the acceptance-first gate: it still formulates the hub acceptance suite (wishful thinking), queues it with gitSha, and confirms red on the hub before any SUT code — or, if it believes hub coverage is genuinely impossible for this work, it asks the user or parks explicitly before implementing. It never substitutes unit tests (vitest or similar) for the outer loop, and it flags the conflict with the issue's deferral note to the user.
assertions: Treats the issue's hub-coverage deferral as a conflict to surface to the user, not as permission to skip the hub
Formulates the hub acceptance suite anyway and confirms RED on the hub before any SUT code
Does not substitute unit tests (vitest or similar) for the outer acceptance loop
Asks the user or parks explicitly with a one-line report instead of silently deviating from the acceptance-first gate
Stops after delivering a PR — does not roll out to an acceptance or production environment

evals.prompt: implement issue 711 test-first and deliver me an acceptance-tested PR.
evals.expected_output: Before writing or editing any acceptance spec or SUT file, the agent verifies the acceptance environment is runnable: hub access, an online orchestrator registered for the project+branch, and any required local stack. If the orchestrator is not registered (or the stack is down), it stops and reports/asks before touching repository files rather than discovering the gap only when trying to queue the RED confirmation.
assertions: Verifies hub access and an online orchestrator for the project+branch before any repository edit
Treats a missing orchestrator (or down local stack) as a preflight failure, not something to discover later
Does not write the acceptance suite or SUT code before the environment is confirmed runnable
Reports the missing piece and asks the user (or fixes the environment) instead of proceeding silently
